questions.question: A car travels 60 meters in 4 seconds at constant velocity. What is its velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity = displacement / time = 60 m / 4 s = 15 m/s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divide distance by time to find velocity.

questions.question: An object starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s^2 for 5 seconds. What is its final velocity?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Multiply acceleration by time when starting from rest.

questions.question: Which graph represents constant acceleration?
questions.correctAnswer: A velocity-time graph with a straight sloped line
distractors: A position-time graph with a horizontal line
A velocity-time graph with a horizontal line
An acceleration-time graph with a curved line
questions.explanation: Constant acceleration means velocity changes at a steady rate, so the v-t graph is a straight line with constant slope.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Constant acceleration means a straight sloped v-t line.

questions.question: A ball is dropped from rest. Ignoring air resistance, how far does it fall in 2 seconds? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Half g times time squared gives the fall distance.

questions.question: A projectile is launched horizontally from a cliff. What is its initial vertical velocity?
questions.explanation: Horizontal launch means the initial velocity is purely horizontal; the vertical component starts at zero.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Horizontal launch starts with zero vertical speed.

questions.question: In projectile motion without air resistance, the horizontal velocity:
questions.explanation: No horizontal force acts, so horizontal velocity never changes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No horizontal force means no horizontal change.

questions.question: At the top of its trajectory, a projectile's vertical velocity is:
questions.explanation: At the peak, the object momentarily stops moving vertically before falling back down.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The peak is where vertical motion pauses.

questions.question: A car accelerates from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 seconds. What is its acceleration?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Change in velocity divided by time is acceleration.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity per time, so meters per second squared.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Acceleration units are meters per second squared.

questions.question: An object moves with constant velocity. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means no change in velocity, so acceleration is zero.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No change in velocity means zero acceleration.

questions.question: A stone is thrown upward at 20 m/s. How long until it reaches its highest point? (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: t = v/g = 20/10 = 2 s at the top where v = 0.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Launch speed divided by g gives time to the top.

questions.question: Two balls are dropped from the same height at the same time, one twice as heavy. Ignoring air resistance, they hit the ground:
questions.explanation: Mass does not affect free-fall acceleration; both accelerate at g.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mass does not matter in free fall.

questions.question: A car travels 100 m in 5 s, then 100 m in 10 s. Its average velocity over the whole trip is:
questions.explanation: Average velocity is total displacement divided by total time. The car keeps moving the same way, so displacement is 100 + 100 = 200 m and time is 5 + 10 = 15 s: 200 / 15 = 13.3 m/s. Do not average 20 m/s and 10 m/s - the car spends longer at the slower speed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Total displacement over total time, not an average of speeds.

questions.question: The area under a velocity-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Area under v-t = velocity times time = displacement.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Area under v-t is displacement.

questions.question: The slope of a position-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Slope of x-t = change in position over time = velocity.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Slope of position-time is velocity.

questions.question: Newton's first law is also called the law of:
questions.explanation: The first law states objects resist changes in motion, which is inertia.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: First law equals inertia.

questions.question: A net force of 20 N acts on a 4 kg mass. Its acceleration is:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Force divided by mass is acceleration.

questions.question: Newton's third law states that forces always occur in:
questions.explanation: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Action-reaction pairs are equal and opposite.

questions.question: The weight of a 10 kg object on Earth (g = 10 m/s^2) is:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Weight is mass times g.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). From F = ma, 1 N is the force that gives 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m/s^2, so 1 N = 1 kg m/s^2.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Force is measured in newtons.

questions.question: A book rests on a table. The normal force on the book is:
questions.explanation: The table pushes up with a force equal to the book's weight, balancing it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The table pushes up exactly as hard as gravity pulls down.

questions.question: Friction always acts in a direction:
questions.correctAnswer: Opposite to motion or attempted motion
questions.explanation: Friction opposes relative motion between surfaces.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Friction fights motion.

questions.question: Static friction is generally:
questions.explanation: It takes more force to start motion than to maintain it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Starting is harder than sliding.

questions.question: A 5 kg block is pulled with 30 N of force and friction is 10 N. Its acceleration is:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Subtract friction first, then divide by mass.

questions.question: An object in free fall experiences only:
questions.explanation: Free fall means gravity is the only force acting.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Free fall means gravity alone.

questions.question: The coefficient of friction depends on:
questions.explanation: Mu is a property of the two surfaces in contact.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Friction coefficient is about the materials.

questions.question: If the net force on an object doubles and mass stays the same, acceleration:
questions.explanation: From F = ma, acceleration is proportional to net force.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Double the force, double the acceleration.

questions.question: A person pushes a wall with 50 N. The wall pushes back with:
questions.explanation: Newton's third law: the reaction is equal in magnitude.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The wall pushes back equally.

questions.question: Tension in a rope pulling a hanging mass at rest equals:
questions.explanation: At rest, tension balances weight exactly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: At rest, tension equals weight.

questions.question: In an elevator accelerating upward, your apparent weight:
questions.explanation: The floor must push harder to accelerate you upward, so the normal force increases.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Upward acceleration feels heavier.

questions.question: Centripetal acceleration always points:
questions.correctAnswer: Toward the center of the circle
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration comes from the change in the direction of velocity as the object moves around the circle. That change points toward the center, so a_c = v^2/r is always directed toward the center.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Centripetal points to the center.

questions.question: The formula for centripetal acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration grows with the square of the tangential speed and shrinks with radius: a_c = v^2/r. Check the units: (m/s)^2 / m = m/s^2, as an acceleration must be.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Centripetal acceleration is speed squared over radius.

questions.question: A car rounds a curve at constant speed. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Direction changes even at constant speed, so there is centripetal acceleration.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Turning means accelerating even at constant speed.

questions.question: If speed doubles while radius stays the same, centripetal force:
questions.explanation: F = mv^2/r, so doubling v quadruples F.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Speed squared means double speed, four times force.

questions.question: The period of uniform circular motion is:
questions.explanation: The period T is the time for one complete revolution. Its partner is frequency: f = 1/T, the number of revolutions per second, so T = 2(pi)r/v for motion at speed v around a circle of radius r.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Period is time per revolution.

questions.question: Newton's law of universal gravitation states force is proportional to:
questions.correctAnswer: The product of the masses divided by distance squared
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gravity follows an inverse-square law.

questions.question: If the distance between two masses doubles, gravitational force becomes:
questions.explanation: Inverse-square: doubling r divides force by 4.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Double the distance, quarter the gravity.

questions.question: A satellite in circular orbit has its centripetal force provided by:
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls the satellite toward Earth, keeping it in orbit.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Orbit is gravity acting as centripetal force.

questions.question: Geosynchronous satellites orbit with a period of:
questions.explanation: They stay above the same spot on Earth, matching Earth's rotation period.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Geosynchronous means matching Earth's day.

questions.question: The gravitational field strength g at Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.explanation: g = 9.8 m/s^2, equivalently 9.8 N/kg.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: g is about 9.8 newtons per kilogram.

questions.question: The SI unit of energy is the:
questions.explanation: Energy is measured in joules (J). One joule is the work done by a 1 N force moving an object 1 m in the force direction, so 1 J = 1 N m.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Energy is measured in joules.

questions.question: Kinetic energy depends on:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Kinetic energy is half mass times speed squared.

questions.question: A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s has kinetic energy of:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Half mass times speed squared.

questions.question: Gravitational potential energy near Earth is:
questions.explanation: PE = mgh for height h above a reference.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Potential energy is mass times g times height.

questions.question: Work is defined as:
questions.correctAnswer: Force times displacement in the direction of the force
questions.explanation: W = Fd cos(theta).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Work is force along the displacement.

questions.question: If a force acts perpendicular to displacement, the work done is:
questions.explanation: cos(90 deg) = 0, so W = 0.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Perpendicular force does no work.

questions.question: Power is:
questions.explanation: P = W/t.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Power is work per time.

questions.question: The SI unit of power is the:
questions.explanation: Power is measured in watts (W). One watt is one joule of work done per second, so 1 W = 1 J/s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Power is measured in watts.

questions.question: A machine does 100 J of work in 5 seconds. Its power is:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Work divided by time is power.

questions.question: The work-energy theorem states that net work equals:
questions.explanation: W_net = delta KE.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Net work changes kinetic energy.

questions.question: In a closed system with only conservative forces, mechanical energy is:
questions.explanation: Without friction or other nonconservative work, KE + PE stays constant.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Conservative forces conserve mechanical energy.

questions.question: A ball dropped from height h hits the ground with speed:
questions.explanation: From energy conservation: mgh = (1/2)mv^2, so v = sqrt(2gh).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Energy conservation gives root 2gh.

questions.question: Elastic potential energy in a spring is:
questions.explanation: Stretching or compressing a spring by x stores PE = (1/2)kx^2. The factor 1/2 appears because the spring force grows from 0 to kx as it stretches, so the average force is kx/2 and the work done is (kx/2)(x).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Spring energy is half k x squared.

questions.question: If speed triples, kinetic energy increases by a factor of:
questions.explanation: KE depends on v^2, so 3^2 = 9.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Triple speed, nine times energy.

questions.question: A pendulum's maximum speed occurs at:
distractors: The midpoint of the swing upward
questions.explanation: At the bottom, all potential energy has become kinetic energy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lowest point means fastest swing.

questions.question: Momentum is defined as:
questions.explanation: p = mv.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Momentum is mass times velocity.

questions.question: The SI unit of momentum is:
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mv, so its unit combines mass and velocity units: kg times m/s, giving kg m/s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Momentum units are kilogram meters per second.

questions.question: Impulse equals:
questions.explanation: J = F delta t = delta p.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Impulse is change in momentum.

questions.question: In a closed system with no external forces, total momentum is:
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum holds without external impulses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No external force means momentum conserved.

questions.question: A 2 kg object moving at 4 m/s collides and sticks to a stationary 2 kg object. Their final speed is:
questions.explanation: Total momentum before = 8 kg m/s; total mass after = 4 kg; v = 8/4 = 2 m/s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sticky collisions share momentum across total mass.

questions.question: An elastic collision conserves both momentum and:
questions.explanation: Elastic means no kinetic energy is lost.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Elastic collisions keep kinetic energy too.

questions.question: Airbags reduce injury by:
questions.correctAnswer: Increasing the time of impact, reducing force
questions.explanation: Same impulse over longer time means smaller force.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Longer impact time means smaller force.

questions.question: A force of 10 N acts for 3 seconds. The impulse is:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Impulse is force times time.

questions.question: Two objects of equal mass collide elastically head-on, one moving and one at rest. After collision, the moving object:
questions.explanation: In an equal-mass elastic collision, velocities exchange.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Equal masses swap velocities elastically.

questions.question: A rocket moves forward by expelling gas backward. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: The rocket-gas system has zero net external force, so momentum is conserved.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Rockets ride on momentum conservation.

questions.question: Torque is:
questions.explanation: Torque = r F sin(theta).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Torque is force times lever arm.

questions.question: The SI unit of torque is:
questions.explanation: Torque is measured in newton-meters (N m), from torque = rF sin(theta): meters times newtons. It is written N m, not J, because torque is a rotational effect, not an amount of energy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Torque is measured in newton-meters.

questions.question: A longer wrench makes loosening a bolt easier because it:
questions.explanation: Longer r means more torque for the same force.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Longer wrench means more torque.

questions.question: For an object in static equilibrium, the net torque must be:
questions.explanation: No rotation means net torque is zero.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: No turning means zero net torque.

questions.question: Rotational inertia depends on mass and:
questions.correctAnswer: How mass is distributed from the axis
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia grows as mass moves farther from the axis.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Farther mass means more rotational inertia.

questions.question: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere of equal mass and radius roll down a ramp. The solid sphere wins because:
questions.explanation: Less rotational inertia means more energy goes to translation, so it accelerates faster.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Less spin inertia means faster rolling.

questions.question: Angular velocity is measured in:
questions.explanation: Angular velocity omega = (change in angle)/(time) is measured in radians per second (rad/s). A full turn is 2(pi) rad, so an object with omega = 2(pi) rad/s completes one revolution every second.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Angular velocity is radians per second.

questions.question: The relationship between linear speed and angular speed is:
questions.explanation: In one period the object travels the circumference 2(pi)r, so v = 2(pi)r/T. Since omega = 2(pi)/T, this gives v = omega r: points farther from the axis move faster at the same spin rate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Linear speed is angular speed times radius.

questions.question: A figure skater pulls her arms in and spins faster due to:
questions.explanation: Smaller moment of inertia means larger angular velocity when L is conserved.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tucking in spins faster by angular momentum.

questions.question: The center of mass of a uniform rod is at its:
questions.explanation: Uniform mass distribution centers at the middle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Uniform rod balances at its middle.

questions.question: The speed of a wave equals:
questions.explanation: v = f lambda.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wave speed is frequency times wavelength.

questions.question: If frequency doubles and wave speed stays constant, wavelength:
questions.explanation: lambda = v/f, so doubling f halves lambda.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Double frequency means half wavelength.

questions.question: The period of a wave is:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Period is one over frequency.

questions.question: Sound waves are:
questions.explanation: Sound travels as compressions and rarefactions along the direction of travel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sound is a longitudinal wave.

questions.question: The Doppler effect is a change in observed frequency due to:
questions.correctAnswer: Relative motion between source and observer
questions.explanation: Motion toward or away shifts the perceived frequency.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Motion shifts the pitch you hear.

questions.question: A wave with greater amplitude carries:
questions.explanation: Energy is proportional to amplitude squared.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bigger amplitude means more energy.

questions.question: When two waves meet and their amplitudes add, it is called:
questions.explanation: In-phase addition builds a larger wave.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Adding waves constructively builds bigger ones.

questions.question: The fundamental frequency of a string fixed at both ends has wavelength:
questions.explanation: The fundamental fits half a wavelength on the string, so lambda = 2L.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fundamental wavelength is twice the string.

questions.question: Sound travels fastest through:
questions.explanation: Particles are closest in solids, transmitting vibrations fastest.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sound is fastest in solids.

questions.question: An echo is an example of:
questions.explanation: Echoes are sound waves bouncing back off a surface.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Echoes are reflected sound.

questions.question: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
questions.explanation: Charge is measured in coulombs (C). Current links charge to time: a flow of 1 C per second is 1 ampere, so 1 C = 1 A s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Charge is measured in coulombs.

questions.question: Electric current is:
questions.explanation: I = Q/t.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Current is charge per time.

questions.question: Ohm's law states:
questions.explanation: Voltage equals current times resistance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Voltage equals current times resistance.

questions.question: A resistor has 6 V across it and 2 A through it. Its resistance is:
questions.explanation: R = V/I = 6/2 = 3 ohms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Voltage divided by current is resistance.

questions.question: In a series circuit, the current is:
questions.explanation: Series has one path, so current is identical throughout.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Series current is the same everywhere.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each branch is:
questions.explanation: Parallel branches connect across the same two points.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Parallel branches share the same voltage.

questions.question: Two 6-ohm resistors in series have equivalent resistance of:
questions.explanation: Series resistances add: 6 + 6 = 12 ohms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Series resistances add up.

questions.question: Two 6-ohm resistors in parallel have equivalent resistance of:
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Parallel halves equal resistances.

questions.question: Electric power can be calculated as:
questions.explanation: P = IV is the general power formula.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Power is current times voltage.

questions.question: A 100 W bulb runs for 2 hours. The energy used is:
questions.explanation: Energy = power times time = 100 x 2 = 200 Wh.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Energy is power times time.

questions.question: Like charges:
questions.explanation: Like charges repel; opposites attract.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Like charges push apart.

questions.question: Coulomb's law states force is proportional to:
questions.correctAnswer: Product of charges divided by distance squared
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Electric force follows an inverse-square law.

questions.question: An electric field is defined as force per unit:
questions.explanation: E = F/q.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Field is force per charge.

questions.question: A capacitor stores energy in:
questions.explanation: Capacitors hold charge separated across plates, storing energy in the field between them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Capacitors store energy in electric fields.

questions.question: The AP Physics 1 exam includes which of the following?
questions.explanation: AP Physics 1 has a multiple-choice section and a free-response section.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: AP Physics 1 mixes multiple-choice and free-response.
